recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants to make header references such as author, attester, or custodian optional rather than SHALL, that would be a new substantive policy decision beyond FHIR-8434's published resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-8434 was Published/Persuasive for the FHIR-core documents page. It objected that document content wording could be interpreted to require every resource referenced by Composition, including author, attester, custodian, and reference-valued extensions, to be present in a document Bundle. The accepted resolution was to trim the wording to list the specific header reference elements rather than simply saying all references, because extensions were not intended to be covered.
initial_application: No FHIR-8434-tagged source commit was found. The Jira comment says the change had already been done for another task. FHIR-8026 and git commit f5bac309ca9e1addc0aaf5c31f99bdaa8d65c6af identify that earlier application: source/documents.html was changed to introduce an explicit generated Composition reference list.
additional_context: Current source/documents.html remains build-scoped as the root documents narrative page, linked from source/documentation.html. The current rendered build expands the generated list to concrete base Composition elements such as Composition.subject, Composition.author, Composition.attester.party, Composition.custodian, Composition.section.focus, and Composition.section.entry, and does not include reference-valued extensions. Later source history, including FHIR-43295, clarified graph/reference mechanics without reversing the explicit-list approach. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source edits. The authoritative current source already satisfies the accepted FHIR-8434 resolution, and indirectly referenced resources are only SHOULD in the surrounding text.
